title: "Sale Price" advertised ABOVE MSRP on every new vehicle
quote: MSRP $54,900 Doc Fee $85 Z Shield $959 Sale Price $55,944
recommendation: Every one of the 10 new-vehicle specials labels the total as "Sale Price" while that number is ~$1,044 ABOVE MSRP (it adds an $85 doc fee and a $959 dealer-installed "Z Shield" add-on). "Sale Price" implies a reduction from a genuine prior/reference price; a figure above MSRP labeled a "sale" price risks misleading a reasonable consumer under §17501. Rename the line to a neutral, accurate label (e.g., "Dealer Price" or "Total Price with Add-Ons") and reserve "Sale Price" for figures at or below a substantiated reference price. Components are itemized (MSRP/Doc/Z Shield/Sale Price), which partially mitigates, hence warning not critical.

title: $959 Z Shield add-on bundled into advertised price without clear "optional/not required" disclosure
quote: Z Shield $959 Sale Price $55,944 ... Vehicles may include dealer add ons such as paint sealant or aftermarket theft devices.
statute: CARS Rule / CA SB 766 (operative 2026-10-01); CA Bus. & Prof. Code §17500
recommendation: Forward-looking (SB 766 operative Oct 1, 2026; today is 2026-07-23, so pre-operative): the $959 dealer-installed "Z Shield" is added into the advertised total on all 10 new vehicles, and the only disclosure is a generic page-level line that add-ons "may" be included. It never states the Z Shield is OPTIONAL and NOT REQUIRED, nor that it can be declined. Before SB 766 takes effect, present the Z Shield as a clearly-optional line item with an explicit "this add-on is optional and not required for purchase" statement adjacent to the price, and default the advertised price to exclude declinable add-ons. Treat as advisory/forward-looking today; it becomes a hard requirement Oct 1, 2026.

title: Used vehicle pages do not reference the CARS Act 3-day cancellation right
quote: Used, Pre-Owned Auto Specials. 10 Matching Vehicles.
statute: CA SB 766 / Car Buyer's Bill of Rights (operative 2026-10-01)
recommendation: NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW AND VERIFICATION — The pre-owned specials page extraction was limited to the listing view (per-VDP and full Terms of Use/policy pages were not fully rendered), so absence of both a cancellation reference AND any contradictory "all sales final"/waiver language could not be fully confirmed. Forward-looking (SB 766 operative Oct 1, 2026, today is pre-operative): the 3-day right to cancel applies to used vehicles $50,000 or less (note several listed units — 740i, 840i, X7 M60i — appear to exceed that threshold). Absence of a website reference is a best-practice/advisory concern, not a violation, per judgment criterion 13; it becomes a stronger concern only if any terms attempt to waive or contradict the right. Recommend adding an accurate 3-day cancellation reference on used VDPs before Oct 1, 2026, and human review of the Terms of Use for any conflicting "all sales final"/waiver language (criterion 15).

title: Non-MSRP "Sale Price" advertised for new BMW vehicles
quote: MSRP $54,900 Doc Fee $85 Z Shield $959 Sale Price $55,944
recommendation: NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW AND VERIFICATION — This requires interpretation of BMW's MAP / price-advertising policy against the site's presentation, which an automated pass cannot definitively adjudicate. BMW-PRICE-002 states "No price advertising other than MSRP for new vehicles." Every new-vehicle special advertises a dealer-constructed "Sale Price" (MSRP + doc fee + $959 Z Shield add-on) rather than MSRP alone. While MSRP is correctly labeled and disclaimed, the prominent non-MSRP "Sale Price" for new vehicles may conflict with BMW's MSRP-only advertising standard and jeopardize co-op eligibility. Recommend BMW co-op/brand-standards review of the new-vehicle pricing presentation.

title: WCAG AA gaps (missing alt text / input label) risk BMW co-op eligibility
quote: images_missing_alt: 4 of 20; inputs_missing_label: 1 of 30 (homepage)
recommendation: NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW AND VERIFICATION — A full WCAG 2.x AA audit (including contrast ratios and heading hierarchy) was not performed; only alt-text/label counts were captured. BMW-WEB-006 requires all BMW web assets to meet WCAG Level AA (incl. 1.1.1 non-text alternatives and 2.4.6 labels). The homepage shows 4 of 20 images without alt text and 1 of 30 inputs without a label. These same gaps are separately captured under the deterministic ADA legal checks; this brand finding flags the distinct BMW co-op / brand-standards consequence. Remediate alt text and input labels and run a full AA audit.

title: "We do not sell" claim inconsistent with ad-personalization and a Do-Not-Sell/opt-out control
quote: We do not sell, rent, or trade consumer personal information to third parties ... [yet] We use cookies and browser activity to improve your experience, personalize content and ads ... Require Opt-Out
statute: CCPA/CPRA, Cal. Civ. Code §1798.100 et seq.
recommendation: NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW AND VERIFICATION — Reconciling the policy's flat "we do not sell/rent/trade" statement with the site's actual data flows requires reviewing the ad/analytics vendors and cookie configuration, which the automated pass could not inspect. The 2020-dated policy states the dealer does not sell PI, yet the cookie notice says the site personalizes "content and ads" and the homepage exposes a "Require Opt-Out / Do Not Sell" control — under CPRA, cross-context behavioral advertising is typically a "sale" or "share" requiring accurate disclosure. This internal inconsistency is a distinct gray-area concern separate from the deterministically-flagged missing rights/GPC gaps. Recommend legal review to align the sell/share disclosure with actual ad-tech practices and update the policy (last updated January 1, 2020, pre-CPRA).
